title: Recursive Environment Scaling for General Long-Horizon Agents
data_curation: Seeds are existing benchmark environments (294 tasks: 105 Claw-Eval-Live, 100 Workspace-Bench-Lite, 89 Terminal-Bench 2.1) plus a ClawGym training task pool. The baseline SFT set takes 8,428 distinct ClawGym tasks, one structurally complete DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash rollout each, deduplicated and filtered for complete messages, matched tool calls/returns and released native score >= 0.8 (3,381 full-score, 5,047 partial; <= 49,152 tokens; 190.52M input / 39.74M target tokens). The RES set applies RES to the same pool and has DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash collect an equal number of new trajectories in the scaled environments under the same rules. Malformed tool calls stay in context but are loss-masked. Overlap checks against all three benchmarks found no matches; manual review of 60 original/scaled pairs found no leakage or scoring bypasses.
curriculum: Not a focus of this paper. Training is a single one-epoch full-parameter SFT stage on Qwen3.5 Base checkpoints (4B, 9B, 35B-A3B) comparing original vs RES trajectories at equal count; the recursive element is in environment construction, where each accepted child environment becomes the parent for the next round (up to depth 10), so difficulty accumulates along a lineage rather than through a training schedule.
method: Recursive Environment Scaling keeps a task's objective, facts and completion requirements fixed and transforms only its executable environment. A proposer (GPT-5.6 Sol, high reasoning effort) inspects the accepted parent E_k and composes a plan from a library of 17 Claw operators (sharding, pagination, field references, numeric re-encoding, export preparation, evidence dispersion, namespace bridges, archive views, index reconstruction, staged release, etc.), changing information access, resource relations and operation dependencies, with dependency composition chaining operators. Execution-grounded validation checks lineage/contract hashes, replays the plan from the frozen parent, and traverses public interfaces in a fresh session to confirm all source facts remain recoverable; failures return diagnostics for repair (budget 8 outer executions per parent). Accepted children are inherited. Lineages stop at depth 10 or after three failed DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash target attempts. SFT: ms-swift, LR 2e-5/1e-5/5e-6 for 4B/9B/35B-A3B, batch 16, 527 updates, 49,152-token max length, 4xH800.
eval_metrics: Claw-Eval-Live (Pass@1 at native score >= 0.80, mean native score), Workspace-Bench-Lite (TCR@80, rubric pass rate RPR) and Terminal-Bench 2.1 (binary verifier Pass@1), each with one 50-turn attempt per task. Six models were evaluated on original vs RES environments; on Claw-Eval-Live Pass@1, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash went 82.86->5.71, GPT-5.6 Sol 85.71->26.67 and Claude Opus 5 86.67->28.57. SFT on RES trajectories, Qwen3.5-35B-A3B: Claw Pass@1 77.14 vs 64.76, Workspace TCR@80 28.00 vs 14.00, Terminal-Bench 38.20 vs 23.60. Ablations: removing dependencies raises Pass@1 0->100% on 15 tasks; no inheritance gives 93.33 vs 6.67; the 6-operator basic library gives 80.00.
key_results: RES lowers success for all six evaluated frontier models on all three benchmarks (by 57.14-77.14 points on Claw-Eval-Live), and with equal trajectory counts SFT on RES trajectories beats original-trajectory SFT in all nine model-benchmark comparisons by 7.00-14.61 points. Accepted children cost on average 1.45 proposer executions, 89.2k tokens and 112.6 s each.
evolution_note: RES sits beside environment-synthesis work (EnvScaler, ScaleEnv, Agent-World) and recursive task synthesis such as RST, but transforms existing benchmark environments in place instead of building new tasks. Holding the objective fixed allows paired original-vs-scaled comparisons. The approach extends saturated benchmarks such as Claw-Eval-Live into harder variants, and the paper shows these variants also serve as a source of long-horizon SFT data.
